question: Using Section 4J.03 and Figure 4J-3, give the full pedestrian-hybrid-beacon sequence and identify which stage corresponds to the pedestrian walk interval.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Per Section 4J.03 and Figure 4J-3, the sequence is: (1) dark until activated; (2) flashing CIRCULAR yellow upon pedestrian actuation; (3) steady CIRCULAR yellow; (4) both steady CIRCULAR RED indications; (5) alternating flashing CIRCULAR RED indications; and (6) dark again until the next actuation. The pedestrian walk interval corresponds to stage 4 — the display of both steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications — while stage 5 (alternating flashing red) corresponds to the pedestrian change interval. Standards (mandatory): - "Following an actuation by a pedestrian, a pedestrian hybrid beacon face shall display a flashing CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by a steady CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by both steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian walk interval, followed by alternating flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian change interval (see Figure 4J-3). Upon … termination of the pedestrian change interval, the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces shall revert to a dark (not illuminated) condition." - "A pedestrian hybrid beacon face shall consist of three signal sections, with a CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indication centered below two horizontally-aligned CIRCULAR RED signal indications (see Figure 4J-3)." - "Except as otherwise provided in this Section, a pedestrian hybrid beacon shall meet the provisions of Chapters 4D through 4G, 4I, and 4J." Options (permitted): - Per the note in Figure 4J-3: "An optional steady red clearance interval may be added after Interval 3, and an optional short buffer interval (alternating flashing red while the pedestrian signal heads are displaying a steady UPRAISED HAND) may be added after Interval 5." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 4J-3 depicts the six numbered intervals of the beacon sequence, explicitly labeling Interval 4 (two illuminated steady red indications, "SR") as "Steady Red During Pedestrian Walk Interval" and Interval 5 (alternating flashing red, "FR") as the pedestrian change interval. [Image 4] shows the full page containing Figure 4J-3 with the legend (SY, FY, SR, FR) and the note on optional clearance and buffer intervals. Citations: - Section 4J.03 Standard §2 (p.730) - Section 4J.02 Standard §2 (p.728) - Section 4J.02 Standard §1 (p.728) - Figure 4J-3 (p.729) - Page 769
gold_answer: Dark, flashing yellow, steady yellow, both steady red, alternating flashing red, then dark. The both-steady-red stage corresponds to the pedestrian walk interval.
